report:
Finding: The difference looks like a strong “culinary/food/restaurant/blog” domain direction in Model B vs. A.

Reasoning:
- Where the signal is: The norm spikes from mid-to-late layers, especially layers ~16–25 and positions 1–4 (e.g., L21 p1–p4, L22 p1–p4), indicating this difference strongly shapes the early continuation.
- What the direction points to: Across those high-norm cells the logit-lens top tokens are dominated by food/culinary terms: “restaurant/Restaurant,” “cooking/Cooking,” “Chef/chef,” “baking/Bake/Baked,” “kitchen,” “Cake,” “Cook,” “Cafe,” “professional/Professional,” “blog/Blog/blogger/blogging,” “Food,” plus related words like “microwave,” “Kitchen,” “Cafe.” This pattern is persistent across many adjacent layers and positions.
- By contrast, earlier/lower-norm cells show a grab-bag of proper nouns/technical terms (“metropolitan,” “chiropractic,” “billionaire,” “doctoral”), but this is not as consistent or concentrated as the culinary theme in the later, high-norm region.

Interpretation:
- Model B appears more biased toward or adapted to culinary/restaurant/blog-style content (e.g., chef/cooking/baking/cake/restaurant/blog vocabulary). This could reflect domain fine-tuning or an added steering vector in that domain.
- I cannot pinpoint a narrower objective (e.g., “recipe generation”) since canonical recipe markers (“Ingredients,” “Directions,” measurements) don’t appear; the signal supports a broader culinary/food media/blog domain shift.
